explanation: Scope is the part of the source where a name can be used. A name declared inside a block is usually visible from its declaration to the end of that block. A second declaration in the same scope can conflict with the first.
exampleExplanation: The inner block can see total. The return statement is outside the block where bonus was declared.
misconceptions: Scope is where a name is visible. Lifetime is how long its object exists.
An inner declaration can hide an outer name. Two incompatible declarations in the same scope are a different situation.

reference.title: Local C reference on block and file scope
reference.text: A name declared inside a compound statement has block scope. A declaration outside all functions has file scope beginning at its declaration. A function parameter in a definition is visible throughout the function body. Start tracing a scope diagnostic at the use or second declaration and look outward through enclosing braces.
